Sampled HR@10 measures ranking within the supplied candidates; it need not preserve full-catalog model rankings, even in expectation ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Keep the pinned users, 99 negatives, seeds and evaluator unchanged, and describe results as benchmark-specific sampled HR@10. Economical comparison: cache each model’s per-user binary hits, compute paired differences against the baseline, then bootstrap users within each category using identical resampled indices for both models; average the four category differences equally. This proposed application follows standard [paired bootstrap semantics](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html) and requires no retraining. Report category scores, macro improvement and an approximate 95% interval. With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125.

Repeatedly choosing hyperparameters or epochs on the same small validation set can overfit the selection criterion; selection bias can rival differences between algorithms ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Practical implication: predeclare a modest search budget and comparison rule, log every attempted configuration, and treat marginal validation wins as exploratory. A paired bootstrap interval for a selected winner does not correct adaptive selection bias or capture training-seed and candidate-sampling uncertainty. Preserve the mandated macro validation selection rule; use uncertainty summaries to qualify evidence, and reserve held-out evaluation for the final selected model.
